inicio.titulo: WebMCP on your site: tools on the page, with fallback and testing
inicio.lead: Register tools with document.modelContext, mark which ones only read and which ones have consequences, make the important action wait for the person, and test everything on its own. WebMCP is a draft from 10/16/2026: the course teaches you to prepare the page without breaking things for people who don't have the API.
inicio.capa_alt: Dark developer desk with a monitor showing a browser and a cable plugged into a small metal hub.

numeros.t: test modes: no API, polyfill, native

inicio.aulas_sub: From the state of the spec to the automatic test battery: environment, first tool, lifecycle, annotations, form, catalog, and testing.

itens: Front-end devs or makers who edit HTML/JS and run commands in the terminal.
People who want their own site to be used by agents in the browser without giving up the normal path.
People who would rather prepare with tests than bet on an API that still changes.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Read the dated spec and tell draft, origin trial, and flag apart.
Register, list, remove, and cancel tools with document.modelContext.
Set annotations and put the action with consequences behind a Confirmar button.
Run the test battery in the no API, polyfill, and native modes, and catch a failure.

blocos.t: Where this course fits in the WebMCP Track
itens: After course 0 (how agents use a site) and course 1 (MCP server).
It owns the WebMCP API on the page. Course 3 looks at the agent side; course 4, at security.
Before you start: Node 20 or newer, git, and disk space for Playwright's Chromium.
